svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Inter, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Deployment and Release Flow — Commit to Production Traffic
Every stage is a Git commit reconciled by Argo CD · a rollout is a traffic change, not a redeploy · rollback lands in under a minute
Image is built, scanned, signed and pushed
docker build · unit tests · vulnerability scan
Gate — no critical CVEs · signature valid · never :latest
Contract checks and a load benchmark must pass before the image may run
health and ready probes · SIGTERM drain · /metrics
Gate — contract passes · the autoscaling numbers become evidence, not guesswork
Deployed with zero real traffic and compared against the incumbent
Gate — error, latency and output comparison acceptable over an agreed sample
A one-line routing.yaml change — nothing is redeployed
Gate — bake window clean · error delta under 0.1% · saturation healthy
Progressive weight increase, each step gated automatically
AMP and Managed Grafana check SLO and saturation
Gate — every step holds its bake window before the next begins (auto-abort on two breaches)
The alias moves; the previous version stays warm as the rollback target
100% of traffic to the new version
Gate — 24 to 72 hour soak clean before the previous version may be retired
Clean up after the retention window, keeping GPU spend bounded
scales the previous version to 0 replicas
Gate — no rollback requested in the window · at most 3 live versions per model
1 · Terraform / OpenTofu PR — plan posted for review
4 · EKS control plane: one minor version at a time
5 · Nodes replaced by Karpenter drift, honouring PDBs
6 · Gateway: N+1 beside N, 10% of routes, then flip
7 · Add-ons and CRDs pinned, upgraded in staging first
Platform changes reach every model, so staging mirrors
production shape and every change reverts through Git.
GPU capacity: hold one AZ of headroom during node work —
stock-outs bite exactly when nodes are being replaced.
previous version still warm for 14 days
no image rebuild, no redeploy, no consumer change
This is the whole reason a version is an immutable workload.
One canary per model at a time
At most 3 live versions: stable, canary, previous
Every change is a reviewable, revertible Git diff
Auto-abort fires on two consecutive gate breaches, so a
noisy sample cannot fail a good version.
GitLab, Argo CD, Kyverno and Terraform are the
non-AWS actors and are named on every stage above.
Deployment is never imperative: nothing is applied by hand, every stage is reproducible from Git, and the same mechanism serves a model rollout and an infrastructure change.
